hypotheses.hypothesis: Discussions where the original argument includes explicit comparisons to established scientific or historical norms are associated with lower view change than those without such comparisons.
hypotheses.h0: Discussions with and without explicit scientific/historical norm comparisons in the OP argument have equal probability of view change.
hypotheses.h1: Discussions whose OP argument has such comparisons have lower probability of delta.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Arguments expressing explicit fear of social rejection or isolation are associated with lower view-change rates than arguments stating beliefs without emotional self-defense.
hypotheses.h0: op_expresses_fear_of_social_rejection has no association with delta.
hypotheses.h1: Posts with op_expresses_fear_of_social_rejection=1 have lower delta rates than posts with 0.
hypotheses.note: The comparison group is all other arguments, not only "beliefs stated without emotional self-defense". The feature is expected to be rare. Linear probability model.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Counter-arguments that cite specific, functioning institutional precedents are associated with a higher probability of view change than those relying on abstract normative principles.
hypotheses.h0: Coefficient of oc_cites_functioning_institutional_precedent is zero (controlling for oc_relies_on_abstract_normative_principle) on delta.
hypotheses.h1: Coefficient of oc_cites_functioning_institutional_precedent is positive for delta, relative to abstract principle reliance.
hypotheses.note: Row-level any-comment features; delta is row-level so comparison is approximate. Both features can co-occur.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Discussions featuring longer precomputed log-transformed discussion length are associated with a higher likelihood of the original poster changing their view.
hypotheses.h0: log_length has no association with delta (coefficient = 0).
hypotheses.h1: Higher log_length is associated with higher probability of delta=1 (coefficient > 0).
hypotheses.note: log_length construction is undocumented; used as supplied. Linear probability model on binary delta.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Discussions where the original argument contains explicit admissions of uncertainty are associated with a higher probability of view change than those asserting absolute certainty.
hypotheses.h0: op_expresses_explicit_uncertainty has no association with delta.
hypotheses.h1: Posts with op_expresses_explicit_uncertainty=1 have higher probability of delta=1 than those with 0.
hypotheses.note: The "absolute certainty" contrast is operationalized as the absence of explicit uncertainty admissions (the reference category). Linear probability model.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Counter-arguments frequently challenging multiple distinct factual premises within the argument are positively associated with view change.
hypotheses.h0: multi_premise_challenge has no association with delta.
hypotheses.h1: Rows where a comment challenges multiple distinct factual premises have a higher probability of delta.
hypotheses.note: "Frequently" operationalized as the presence of at least one comment challenging 2+ distinct factual premises (threshold fixed a priori). Linear probability model.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Discussions where the original argument contains fewer counter-argument responses are associated with a lower likelihood of the original poster changing their view.
hypotheses.h0: num_counter_comments has no association with delta.
hypotheses.h1: Higher num_counter_comments is associated with higher delta (fewer comments, lower likelihood).
hypotheses.note: Hypothesis wording says the "original argument contains" counter-argument responses; interpreted as the number of counter-argument comments in OC_comments for the discussion. Linear probability model.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Discussions with at least three distinct counter-arguments in the posted comments are associated with a higher likelihood of the original poster changing their view.

hypotheses.note: Distinct counter-arguments proxied by number of comments in OC_comments (each comment treated as one counter-argument). Linear probability model.
